title: Rethink sort & filter toolbar and compact row mode for large tables
creator: Sophie Nguyen
description: Problem: Our current table header UX for large, virtualized datasets mixes persistent filter controls, column actions, and multi-column sort affordances into a cramped single row. This creates discoverability problems, keyboard-accessibility friction, and poor density behavior for users who need compact views (high-row-count dashboards) versus spacious analytic views. Goal: Design a modular header/toolbar pattern and compact row density that: 1) separates persistent table-wide filters from per-column controls, 2) supports multi-column sorting with clear keyboard and screen-reader cues, 3) introduces a fluid compact density mode optimized for 6+ rows per viewport while preserving targetable hit areas for resize/drag, and 4) ships with tokens/specs for the design system and a Figma component kit that engineering can implement in the virtualized table layer.
acceptance_criteria: A modular header pattern with two zones: persistent toolbar (global filters, search, saved views) and column action row (sort/menu/resize handles), documented with specs and responsive breakpoints.
Compact density mode defined with token values for row-height, padding, and typography, tested with real datasets to validate readability at 6 and 12 rows per viewport.
Accessible keyboard flows for: focus moving into header, multi-column sort composition (shift+click/keyboard), opening column menus, and using resize via keyboard handles. ARIA attributes documented.
Column resize UI uses a larger virtual touch target with a subtle drag overlay and snap hints at common widths. Interaction microcopy and animation durations provided.
Figma component kit delivered (header zones, compact rows, keyboard state frames) and a handoff doc linking to an implementation spike in ENG-4125.
Usability sign-off after 3 lightweight remote sessions covering visual density, discoverability of filters, and keyboard/screen-reader flows.
Engineering acceptance criteria: unit tests for keyboard navigation, visual regression snapshots for compact and regular density, and perf check that virtualization metrics do not regress beyond 5%.
